analysis.one_liner: Cummins India makes diesel and natural-gas engines, generator sets and related power systems, majority-owned by its US parent Cummins Inc., selling into trucks, construction equipment, data centres, manufacturing and distributed power-backup markets.
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (quarter to Sep 2026) came out on 4 November 2026: standalone revenue rose 4.1% YoY to ₹3,301 crore, below analyst estimates, while EBITDA fell 27% to ₹507 crore as the margin collapsed from 21.94% to 15.36%. Standalone PAT fell roughly 27% YoY to ₹467 crore. The stock fell as much as 10-14% intraday on 5 November and slipped further on 6 November, touching a 52-week low near ₹3,878. Management is holding an open-access earnings call on 16 November 2026 to discuss the H1 FY27 numbers in detail.
analysis.plain_terms: This is the Indian arm of a large American engine maker, and it is debt-free with very high returns on capital - on paper, a quality business. But the just-released quarter shows revenue still growing (+4%) while profit fell sharply (~27%), because raw material and freight costs rose faster than prices, and the product mix sold was less profitable. That is a margin problem, not a demand problem - management says customer demand (data centres, factories, real estate) stayed healthy. The market reacted hard, knocking the stock down double digits in two sessions, which tells you investors had priced in much better margins than the company delivered.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) was a record quarter by revenue: standalone sales of ₹3,375 crore, up 18% YoY, but profit before exceptional items was already down slightly YoY and 12% QoQ on rising commodity/freight costs - an early warning the market largely shrugged off. Q2 FY27 (Sep 2026) showed the same pressure intensify: revenue +4.1% YoY to ₹3,301 crore (domestic +5%, exports +2%), but EBITDA margin fell 658 bps to 15.36% from 21.94%, and standalone PAT fell ~27% YoY to ₹467 crore. One source reported consolidated PAT down a smaller 18.5% - that is a different (consolidated) base, not a contradiction of the standalone figure, so treat the two as separate numbers rather than averaging them. A single outlier source described 'PAT down 18% to ₹507 crore', but ₹507 crore matches the EBITDA figure reported elsewhere, suggesting that source conflated EBITDA with PAT - set aside. Management's stated cause: commodity cost inflation, higher freight, and an adverse product mix, not weak demand.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 32.3% from its 27 May 2026 peak of ₹5,977.92, largely because of the Q2 results-driven selloff in early November - this is an earnings-driven fall, not a corporate action; the only recorded corporate action is a 1.4x split back in 2011, which has no bearing on the current price series. Over 1 year the stock is down 4.98% against a flat Nifty (-1.88%) but has badly lagged peer Kirloskar Oil Engines, which is up 60.7% over the same period. That gap widens looking further out: over 3 years the stock is up 148% versus the peer's 194%, and over 5 years up 377% versus the peer's 744%. So this has comfortably beaten the index but has been a clear long-term laggard against its closest listed peer.
analysis.valuation_read: At a P/E of roughly 55-57x (sources cluster in this range), the stock trades well above its own 10-year median of around 37-38x, even after the 32% correction from its peak. Why it looks expensive: the market has historically paid up for Cummins India's debt-free balance sheet and high capital efficiency (ROE ~29.45%, ROCE ~38.64%), both above sector benchmarks. Whether it is actually cheap now is a separate question - the current multiple still assumes margins recover well above the 15.36% just posted, so the de-rating so far may not be the market's final word if the margin pressure persists into Q3.
analysis.growth_read: This is currently volume-led growth with margin-led deterioration layered on top, the two pulling in opposite directions. Revenue did grow in both Q1 (+18% YoY, a record quarter) and Q2 (+4.1% YoY), and management says underlying demand from data centres, manufacturing, realty and the distribution business stayed healthy. But profit fell because input costs outran pricing and the mix shifted - a margin problem sitting on top of real volume growth, which is a different and generally more fixable issue than a demand slowdown.
analysis.health_read: Balance sheet health is strong: the company is reported debt-free (₹0 crore debt), with ROE of ~29.45% and ROCE of ~38.64%, both above peer-group benchmarks. The current pressure is a business/operating-cost risk - commodity and freight inflation plus product mix - not a financial-risk or leverage concern. Whether recent profit is converting cleanly into operating cash flow was not verified in this pass - check on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Cummins Inc. (the US parent) holds a stable 51% stake with 0% pledged, so there is no pledging risk on the register. Institutional holding stood near 40.35% as of the June 2026 quarter, split between FII/FPI (~21.19%, rising) and domestic mutual funds (~12.55%, roughly flat). No well-known individual investor was found on the shareholding register in this search - if one is expected, it does not appear to be currently present based on available data.
strengths: Debt-free balance sheet (₹0 crore reported debt) with ROE of ~29.45% and ROCE of ~38.64%
Record quarterly revenue of ₹3,375 crore in Q1 FY27, up 18% YoY, showing underlying demand strength
Promoter holding stable at 51% with zero pledging - no leverage risk sitting with the controlling shareholder
Revenue still grew 4.1% YoY in Q2 FY27 even as margins compressed, implying the core demand problem management described is cost-side, not volume-side
watchpoints: EBITDA margin fell 658 bps YoY to 15.36% in Q2 FY27 from 21.94% - the key number to watch for a reversal in coming quarters
Stock has badly lagged peer Kirloskar Oil Engines over 1, 3 and 5 years (-4.98% vs +60.7% over 1Y; +377% vs +744% over 5Y)
Trailing P/E of ~55-57x remains well above the 10-year median of ~37-38x even after the 32% drawdown from the May 2026 peak
Q2 revenue missed analyst estimates by ~6.7% and margin missed by ~415 bps - a sign Street estimates may still need to come down further
analysis.one_thing: Whether the EBITDA margin recovers back toward the 20%+ band seen a year ago (versus 15.36% in Q2 FY27) - that resolves whether this is a one-off commodity/freight cost shock or a more structural reset, and the 16 November 2026 earnings call plus the Q3 FY27 print (due around Jan-Feb 2027) are the next checkpoints.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q2 FY27 revenue (+4.1% YoY to ₹3,301 crore) and EBITDA margin contraction (21.94% to 15.36%) across multiple independent sources with consistent figures. Standalone PAT decline clusters around 26-27% to ₹467 crore; one source (scanx.trade) reported PAT down 18% to ₹507 crore, which appears to have mistaken the EBITDA figure for PAT and was set aside as an outlier rather than averaged in. A separately reported consolidated PAT decline of ~18.5% uses a different base than the standalone figure and should not be read as contradicting it. P/E was reported between 55.34x (GuruFocus, as of 4 Nov 2026) and 57.43x (another source, as of 7 Oct 2026) - used as a range. Could not verify operating cash flow conversion or the presence/absence of any specific named individual investor on the shareholding register.
